items.title: MECH-492: does MECH-286's sleep-permission threat conjunct discriminate place safety under both z_harm_a sourcing modes?
items.note: MECH-492 falsifier -- first ever test of this claim (registered 2026-08-14, candidate). Measures whether MECH-286's third gate conjunct (z_harm_a.norm() < 0.4) discriminates place safety, under BOTH z_harm_a sourcing modes, by walking a live agent through real world positions with known ground-truth hazard and reading the gate's OWN emitted diagnostics. NO ree_core change; the gate already emits all three fields. V3-EXQ-891 was deliberately NOT reused as the harness: it set the threat signal by hand (agent._current_latent = SimpleNamespace(z_harm_a=v), line 182) and never ran the encoder or touched ground truth -- exactly the degenerate form MECH-492's what_would_answer forbids. Criteria are transcribed verbatim from what_would_answer, incl. the (C1 xor C2) leg that confirms the claim in its exact registered form; see combination_rule in the manifest -- a 'passed: false' on C1/C2 is a POSITIVE finding for this claim, not a failed run. | GOV-REUSE-1 (Step 2.4): decisive readout is mech286_threat_ok correlated against per-position ground-truth hazard. Grepped every manifest in evidence/experiments/ for 'mech286_threat_ok' and 'mech286_z_harm_a_norm' -- ZERO hits, so the readout is neither recorded nor post-hoc derivable (no run has ever emitted the gate's diagnostics). Not recoverable -> run. | Step 2.5c substrate-path overlap: SD-MECH303-THRESHOLD-SOURCING (severity DEGRADING, open) overlaps ree_core/{utils/config.py,environment/causal_grid_world.py,agent.py} -- recorded per the gate's degrading rule; it is in fact the very sourcing defect this claim is derived from, so the run happens under it by design, not despite it. Two CORRUPTING entries also list overlapping files (mode-governance-engagement: agent.py/config.py/salience_coordinator.py; contextmemory-write-path-addressing-degeneracy: e1_deep.py), both implemented_pending_validation. Proceeded after VERIFYING neither can reach the decisive readout: (i) z_harm_a = AffectiveHarmEncoder.encoder(cat([harm_obs_a, harm_history])) is a pure feedforward function of the OBSERVATION (latent/stack.py:259) with no E1/ContextMemory and no salience-coordinator path; (ii) the environment is stepped with a RANDOM action, so nothing downstream of E1/E3 can influence which positions are visited either. Mode governance is not enabled by this driver. | DV-SYMMETRY DECLARATION (both arms). DV = AUC of the gate's threat_ok (and of -norm) against a binary place-safety label; an AUC/rank DV's symmetry group is monotone rescaling of the score plus permutation of samples within a class. The manipulation (limb_damage_enabled) is NOT invariant under either: it swaps which observation vector feeds the harm encoder (body-damage state, dim 7, vs proximity-EMA field, dim 50), giving a different score with a different position-dependence -- not a monotone transform of the same score. Measured in this session's Step 2.5a probe: damage_sourced norm range 0.0018 over 40 ticks vs proximity_ema 0.400. Separately, threat_ok is a FIXED-ABSOLUTE-threshold boolean, so it is not invariant under monotone rescaling either -- which is precisely the claim's point about an uncalibrated absolute threshold. | SCOPED OUT (not scored, per the 785 structural-vacuity rule): what_would_answer's third, ALSO-FALSIFYING 'another conjunct is always binding' criterion. Measured -- with the gate and its named dependent flags all enabled, the hippocampal staleness accumulator's snapshot stays EMPTY across 400 ticks of the full pipeline, so mech286_staleness_max is identically 0.0 and staleness_ok is structurally False every tick. That makes the staleness conjunct trivially always-binding for a WAKE-ONLY-HARNESS reason, not a gate property; reporting a narrowing verdict off it would be a vacuous gate. threat_ok is computed upstream of and independently of the AND, so the primary measurement is unaffected. A real sleep-loop driver with episode-end notifications is what would answer it -- follow-on, not built here. | ROADS NOT TAKEN (recorded per headless-worker rule 7): (a) no experiments/_lib/baselines/ module was created -- there is no OFF/baseline arm here (both arms are the manipulation), and adding a file under _lib/** would bust the substrate_hash of every existing arm-reuse mint fleet-wide for no reuse gain; cells are instead emitted cross-driver-reusable via include_driver_script_in_hash=False (mint-as-you-go), with all five readout-affecting module constants declared in the config_slice to preclude a false cache HIT. (b) No separate baseline-mint job queued -- neither sanctioned exception applies (no planned parallel consumer; runs on cloud, so no Mac machine-class escape). (c) Encoder deliberately left UNTRAINED, matching the V3-EXQ-917 precedent whose AUC band this claim cites, so auc_neg_norm is directly readable against 917's 0.84-0.97 / <=0.52; a trained-encoder replication is named follow-on. | DO NOT build a MECH-286 fix off this result -- separate follow-on. Note that chip-20260814-mech303-proximity-signal-focused (DONE) already built MECH-303 a dedicated obs_safety_proximity / contextual_safety_gate_source signal, so a future build session re-pointing MECH-286 at that same mechanism has a ready target. | Smoke PASS (--dry-run, 2 seeds x 60 ticks x 2 modes); validate_experiments.py --strict --paths: 1 OK, 0 non-conforming, 0 warnings.
